title: Node/Room Rendering Implementation Plan (Cell + Beam Framing)

notes: The plan now treats every room as a collection of grid cells anchored by beams and framing elements.
Framing beams act as termination points for drywall skin to carve openings (doors/windows) exactly like real construction.
Cell+Beam Graph gate verified—shared adjacency, canonical faces, and beam descriptors came from deterministic cell graph logic.
The room body should be simplified to one procedural thick wall volume between beams rather than separate inner and outer wall layers.

inspiration.description: Procedural emergence dictated by structural constraints; the skin is a procedural membrane stretched between beam endpoints.

axiomatic: A room equals the boolean intersection of floors, ceilings, and walls defined by the grid + beam graph.
Beams and framing elements outline the structural limits and inform where the procedural skin may or may not span.
Each wall boundary should resolve into one thick procedural wall volume between beams, not separate inner and outer wall entities.
axiological: Procedural emergence: adding cells automatically reuses shared beams for shared walls instead of duplicating geometry.
Structural honesty: rendered visuals are a direct byproduct of the beam graph covering all load-bearing/frame elements.
Reduced structural complexity: one canonical thick wall between beams is easier to reason about than dual wall shells.
teleological: Deliver a living tower simulation where cells, beams, framing, and thick procedural wall volumes recompute instantly as rooms change, enabling continuous architectural response.

scope: Represent each room as a set of grid cells with associated beam endpoints at every corner.
Use beam definitions to construct shared walls, floors, and ceilings; framing beams carve openings for doors/windows.
Drive the skin (drywall/glass) from the beam/framing graph so it only ever spans sanctioned surfaces.
Emit adjacency metadata for future procedural placement and selection indicators that follow structural faces.
Keep all modules feature-sliced (grid logic, beam graph, wall volume generation, skin shader) and deterministic.
Model each boundary as a single thick wall volume between beams, with openings carved directly from that wall body.

workstreams.name: Cell + Beam Graph
goals: Map every room to a contiguous set of grid cells.
Generate beams at every cell corner along horizontal/vertical planes so shared walls are captured.
Make beams directional (wall, floor, ceiling) and track adjacency when cells expand or shrink.

phases.name: Cell graph modeling
tasks: Store cell footprints for each room/node in a serializable graph.
Calculate negative-space indicators for cells that share walls (so the skin can merge them).
Track canonical faces per room using cell orientation metadata.

phases.name: Beam endpoint generation
tasks: For each occupied cell, produce beams at its four corners (capsules/boxes) spanning top/bottom and vertical edges.
Share beams between rooms when cells are adjacent so walls reuse the same structural primitive.
Tag beams with roles (interior partition, exterior wall, floor/ceiling) for skin shaders to interpret.

criteria: Every room has a deterministic cell footprint and beam endpoint list.
Adjacency metadata records shared beams so expanding rooms do not double-draw walls.
Canonical face references (front, back, ceiling, floor) derive from the beam graph.

workstreams.name: Framing Beams + Openings
goals: Introduce framing beams (smaller beams) around constrained openings to keep drywall from spanning them.
Model doors/windows as explicit negative spaces bounded by framing so the skin understands where not to render.
Allow framing beams to adapt as rooms grow/shrink on the grid.

phases.name: Framing beam generation
tasks: Define framing beam primitives for door headers, sills, and jambs at cell boundaries.
Respond to opening metadata (width/height/placement) by placing framing beams along to prevent skin overlap.
Expose framing beam IDs so shaders or renderers can treat them as cutout boundaries.

phases.name: Opening metadata and validation
tasks: Validate openings stay contained within the span of the surrounding beams.
Ensure the framing graph reconnects automatically when openings close or relocate.
Provide explicit adjacency data for placement logic (no door should be placed without framing beams).

criteria: Framing beams prevent the skin from spanning openings; the graph data clearly shows cutout boundaries.
Opening validation prohibits dangling beams or uncovered gaps.
Shaders/renderers can query framed openings to adjust materials (glass vs drywall).

workstreams.name: Single Thick Wall Volume
goals: Replace dual inner/outer wall layering with one canonical thick wall volume between beams.
Derive visible faces from the wall body instead of modeling separate wall shells.
Carve openings directly from the wall volume while preserving framing and adjacency semantics.

phases.name: Wall volume contract
tasks: Define a single wall primitive per beam span with explicit thickness.
Store openings, thickness, and face metadata on the wall body instead of duplicated surfaces.
Remove assumptions that walls need separate inner and outer structural objects.

phases.name: Wall volume generation
tasks: Generate thick wall geometry from beam endpoints and span bounds.
Subtract openings and preserve reveal geometry around door/window cutouts.
Keep face shading and visibility as a render-time concern rather than a second wall model.

criteria: Rooms render from one thick wall volume per boundary instead of paired inner/outer walls.
Openings are carved from the wall body without mutating beam framing data.
Wall thickness is procedural and consistent across all room spans.

workstreams.name: Skin (Drywall) Visualization and Selection
goals: Render wall faces from the single thick wall volume and beam/framing metadata.
Use beam/framing metadata to inform shader-driven materials (concrete, drywall, glass) and cutaway logic.
Tie selection overlays and adjacency-based features (procedural placement, cutaways) to structural faces derived from this graph.

phases.name: Drywall skin generator
tasks: Build shader or mesh logic that drapes drywall across the canonical wall volume derived from beams.
Create exterior skin surfaces representing facade walls using exterior beams.
Allow the skin to respond to framing by leaving door/window holes open.

phases.name: Selection & adjacency overlays
tasks: Anchor selection indicators to structural faces computed from the beam graph so they align to visible walls.
Expose adjacency data for future procedural furnishing so placement avoids framing zones.
Keep cutaway visibility non-destructive and derived from the beam/skin graph.

criteria: Wall faces render from a single thick wall volume with openings carved by framing beams.
Selection overlays always reference structural faces instead of fixed offsets.
Adjacency metadata surfaces placement zones for future procedural decorators.

qualityGuards: No duplicate walls—shared beams must be resolved via adjacency metadata.
Framing beams feed the skin shader so drywall never spans door/window gaps.
Structure, beam generation, wall volume generation, and skin rendering remain feature-sliced modules.
Cutaways and selection overlays never mutate the canonical structure graph.
Each wall boundary should have one canonical thick wall body, not separate inner and outer shells.
definitionOfDone: Rooms render from grid cells + beams + framing loops in accordance with rooms-source-of-truth.
Doors/windows remain true negative spaces because framing beams terminate the wall volume.
Selection and procedural placement use adjacency metadata derived from the beams.
Each workstream’s completion check reports `complete` once its criteria are satisfied.
Wall thickness is represented by one procedural wall body per boundary rather than paired wall layers.
